glossdef.p: The Power Supply Unit converts wall outlet power into power for your machine. It connects to your motherboard and has additional connectors for other components such as hard drives and GPUs. A modular PSU means that cables can be removed as needed, making cable management much easier and airflow better at a small premium.

How much wattage you will need for your PSU depends on the components in your system. You can add up the total power draw from each component, which will be listed in each component’s technical manual, and then add extra wattage to help with efficiency. Power supplies are typically most efficient at around 50% of nominal capacity, so if your total power draw is 300 watts then a 600-watt PSU will be most efficient. A PSU constantly operating near maximum load will generate a lot of heat and require noisy fans to cool, and will also wear out faster and put your system at risk.

It is very important to get a trusted, high-quality PSU. Defects in your PSU can lead to your whole system being destroyed by power surges. Do not reuse a PSU, and try to remind yourself to replace your PSU every five years or so, especially on high end systems. An “80 Plus” rating can be an indicator of quality and efficiency. When buying a PSU don’t rely on just the brand name, look at the overall reviews for each model.
